title.en: Author, setting and the two friends

heading.en: Two girls, one school gate, two futures

hook.en: Two school-leavers stand at the same gate. One plans a sensible job; the other dreams of shops, stages and stardom. Going Places asks which of them is really going places.

objectives.en: Introduce A. R. Barton and the setting of the story
Compare Sophie and Jansie as characters
Understand the opening conflict between dream and reality

narration.en: Two school-leavers stand at the same gate. One plans a sensible job; the other dreams of shops, stages and stardom. Going Places asks which of them is really going places.

body.en: Going Places is a short story by A. R. Barton, a modern writer. It is set in a small, working-class town, where most young people leaving school are expected to take up factory work. The story follows Sophie, a teenage girl, as her daydreams run far ahead of her real life.

title.en: Sophie and Jansie: a character map

narration.en: Let us map the two friends and see how differently they think about the future.

say.en: In the centre we write the two school-leavers.
Sophie is the dreamer. Her mind is always somewhere glamorous and far away.
Jansie is her practical friend. She knows what life usually offers girls like them.
Sophie talks of owning a boutique, then of acting or fashion design.
Jansie reminds her that they are both likely to end up working in the biscuit factory.
Jansie points out that a shop needs money, which neither family has.
The gap between wishing and what is possible is the heart of the story.

body.en: Sophie and Jansie are classmates and friends, but they are opposites. Jansie is down-to-earth and accepts the limits of their background, while Sophie refuses to accept them and escapes into fantasy. Jansie acts as the voice of reality that the dreamer keeps brushing aside.

points.en: Sophie: imaginative, impatient with ordinary life
Jansie: sensible, a little nosy, grounded
Their talk sets up the dream-reality conflict

problem.en: How are Sophie and Jansie different in their attitude to the future?

steps.en: Describe Sophie: a dreamer who imagines a boutique and a glamorous career.
Describe Jansie: practical, expecting the factory job that awaits them.
Conclude: one escapes into fantasy, the other accepts reality.

answer.en: Sophie dreams of owning a boutique or becoming an actress or designer, ignoring her limited means. Jansie is practical and knows both of them are likely to work in the biscuit factory. Sophie escapes into fantasy; Jansie accepts reality.
